arxiv-1705-02306.title: Gradient of eigenvalues of Dirac operators and its applications
arxiv-1705-02306.description: Abstract For Dirac operators, which have discrete spectra, the concept of eigenvalues’ gradient is given and formulae for this gradients are obtained in terms of normalized eigenfunctions. It’s shown how the gradient is being used to describe isospectral operators or when finite number of spectral data is changed.

arxiv-1811-02849.title: Thermophysical Modeling of Asteroid Surfaces using Ellipsoid Shape Models Journal: Astronomical Journal
arxiv-1811-02849.creator: Eric M. MacLennan, Joshua P. Emery
arxiv-1811-02849.description: Abstract Thermophysical Models (TPMs), which have proven to be a powerful tool in the interpretation of the infrared emission of asteroid surfaces, typically make use of a priori obtained shape models and spin axes for use as input boundary conditions.

arxiv-2104-02872.title: Harmless label noise and informative soft-labels in supervised classification
arxiv-2104-02872.creator: Daniel Ahfock, Geoffrey J. McLachlan
arxiv-2104-02872.description: Abstract Manual labelling of training examples is common practice in supervised learning. When the labelling task is of non-trivial difficulty, the supplied labels may not be equal to the ground-truth labels, and label noise is introduced into the training dataset.

arxiv-2204-07133.title: FUNDAMENTAL SOLUTION OF THE VLADMIROV-TAIBLESON OPERATOR ON NONCOMMUTATIVE VILENKIN GROUPS Thanks: The authors are supported by the FWO Odysseus 1 grant G.0H94.18N: Analysis and Partial Differential Equations.
arxiv-2204-07133.creator: Julio Delgado and J.P. Velasquez-Rodriguez
arxiv-2204-07133.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Julio Delgado and J.P. Velasquez-Rodriguez. The fundamental solution and the heat semigroup of the Vladimirov-Taibleson operator on constant-order noncommutative Vilenkin groups are obtained, together with some estimates on the associated heat kernel. We also show the existence of a fundamental solution for the ”Vladimirov Laplacian” on the p p -adic Heisenberg group and the p p -adic Engel group, and discuss possible extensions of our results to more general homogeneous operators on graded p p -adic Lie groups.

arxiv-2207-01756.title: Universal Domain Adaptive Object Detector
arxiv-2207-01756.creator: Wenxu Shi 1 , Lei Zhang 1( 🖂 ) , Weijie Chen 2 , Shiliang Pu 2 1 Learning Intelligence & Vision Essential (LiVE) Group 1 School of Microelectronics and Communication Engineering, Chongqing University, China 2 Hikvision Research Institute {wxshi,leizhang}@cqu.edu.cn, {chenweijie5,pushiliang.hri}@hikv
arxiv-2207-01756.description: Abstract Universal domain adaptive object detection (UniDAOD) is more challenging than domain adaptive object detection (DAOD) since the label space of the source domain may not be the same as that of the target and the scale of objects in the universal scenarios can vary dramatically (i.e, category shift and scale shift ).

arxiv-2302-13698.title: Universe bouncing its way to inflation
arxiv-2302-13698.creator: Manjeet Kaur, Debottam Nandi, Debajyoti Choudhury, T. R. Seshadri
arxiv-2302-13698.description: Abstract Cosmological models with inflation and those with bounce have their own strengths and weaknesses. Here we construct a model in which a phase of bounce is followed by a viable inflationary phase. This incorporates several advantages of both and hence, is a more viable model for cosmic evolution.

arxiv-2305-17561.title: Grounding Characters and Places in Narrative Texts
arxiv-2305-17561.creator: Sandeep Soni, Amanpreet Sihra, Elizabeth F. Evans, Matthew Wilkens, David Bamman
arxiv-2305-17561.description: Abstract Tracking characters and locations throughout a story can help improve the understanding of its plot structure. Prior research has analyzed characters and locations from text independently without grounding characters to their locations in narrative time. Here, we address this gap by proposing a new spatial relationship categorization task.

arxiv-2310-17813.title: A Spectral Condition for Feature Learning
arxiv-2310-17813.creator: Greg YangxAI, James B. SimonUC Berkeley & Imbue, Jeremy BernsteinMIT
arxiv-2310-17813.description: Abstract The push to train ever larger neural networks has motivated the study of initialization and training at large network width. A key challenge is to scale training so that a network’s internal representations evolve nontrivially at all widths, a process known as feature learning .

arxiv-2403-09013.title: Impacts of Point Defects on Shallow Doping in Cubic Boron Arsenide: A First Principles Study
arxiv-2403-09013.creator: Shuxiang Zhou 1, Zilong Hua 1 , Kaustubh K. Bawane 1 , Hao Zhou 2 , and Tianli Feng 2
arxiv-2403-09013.description: Abstract Cubic boron arsenide (BAs) stands out as a promising material for advanced electronics, thanks to its exceptional thermal conductivity and ambipolar mobility. However, effective control of p- and n-type doping in BAs poses a significant challenge, mostly as a result of the influence of defects.

arxiv-2404-03005.title: Optimal Reconstruction of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations for DESI 2024
arxiv-2404-03005.creator: and H. Zou
arxiv-2404-03005.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by and H. Zou. Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) provide a robust standard ruler to measure the expansion history of the Universe through galaxy clustering. Density-field reconstruction is now a widely adopted procedure for increasing the precision and accuracy of the BAO detection.

arxiv-2508-19331.title: Towards a few percent measurement of the Hubble constant with the current network of gravitational wave detectors without using electromagnetic information
arxiv-2508-19331.creator: Tom Bertheas, Vasco Gennari, Nicola Tamanini
arxiv-2508-19331.description: Abstract Gravitational waves provide a novel and independent measurement of cosmological parameters, offering a promising avenue to address the Hubble tension alongside traditional electromagnetic observations. In the absence of electromagnetic counterparts or complete host galaxy catalogs, current measurements rely on population-based methods that statistically combine black hole merger events.

arxiv-2510-19981.title: FutrTrack: A Camera-LiDAR Fusion Transformer for 3D Multiple Object Tracking
arxiv-2510-19981.creator: Martha Teiko Teye 1,2 , Ori Maoz 2 Matthias Rottmann 3 1 University of Wuppertal, Germany 2 Aptiv, Germany 3 Institute of Computer Science, Osnabruck University, Germany martha.teye@aptiv.com, ori.maoz@aptiv.com, matthias.rottmann@uos.de
arxiv-2510-19981.description: Abstract We propose FutrTrack, a modular camera-LiDAR multi-object tracking framework that builds on existing 3D detectors by introducing a transformer-based smoother and a fusion-driven tracker. Inspired by query-based tracking frameworks, FutrTrack employs a multi-modal two-stage transformer refinement and tracking pipeline.

pmc-10590161.title: The reproductive status determines tolerance and resistance to Mycobacterium marinum in Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-10590161.creator: Marta Arch, Maria Vidal, Esther Fuentes, Anmaw Shite Abat, Pere-Joan Cardona
pmc-10590161.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sex and reproductive status of the host have a major impact on the immune response against infection. Our aim was to understand their impact on host tolerance or resistance in the systemic Mycobacterium marinum infection of Drosophila melanogaster. We measured host survival and bacillary load at time of death, as well as expression by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction of immune genes (diptericin and drosomycin).

pmc-10649139.title: Predicting Potentially Fatal COVID-19 Disease in Pregnant Patients Using the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR)
pmc-10649139.creator: Dorina Supák, Balázs Mészáros, Balázs Turi, Zoltán Herold, Zoltán Kukor, Sándor Valent
pmc-10649139.description: Objective: To evaluate the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) values’ possible predictive role in fatal and severe cases of COVID-19 disease in pregnant women. Design and data collection: A case-control study was conducted with the inclusion of 45 pregnant COVID-19 patients. All the data were obtained from the hospital information system of Semmelweis University by two of the authors.

pmc-10662518.title: Emergency department utilization in elderly patients: a report from the National Emergency Department Information System (NEDIS) of Korea, 2018-2022
pmc-10662518.creator: Sun Young Lim, You Hwan Jo, Seongjung Kim, Eunsil Ko, Young Sun Ro, Jungeon Kim, Sumin Baek
pmc-10662518.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectiveWith general aging of the population, emergency department (ED) utilization by elderly patients is increasing. In this study, we analyzed data on ED visits of patients aged 65 years and older in Korea.MethodsThe study is a retrospective analysis of National Emergency Department Information System (NEDIS) data from 2018–2022, focusing on patients aged 65 years and older who visited EDs across Korea. ED utilization data were analyzed using Korean Triage and Acuity Scale (KTAS) scores.

pmc-11363069.title: The role of trained immunity in sepsis
pmc-11363069.creator: Wenjuan Wang, Lisi Ma, Bin Liu, Liangliang Ouyang
pmc-11363069.description: Sepsis is defined as a life-threatening organ dysfunction syndrome caused by dysregulated host response to infection, characterized by a systemic inflammatory response to infection. The use of antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, and organ support therapy has limited prognostic benefit in patients with sepsis, and its incidence is not diminishing, which is attracting increased attention in medicine.

pmc-11440571.title: Nutritional status and its associated factors among infants and young children aged 6–23 months in Addis Ababa, Central Ethiopia, 2021: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11440571.creator: Sisay Hailu, Dube Jara, Eyob Ketema Bogale
pmc-11440571.description: The aim of this study is to assess nutritional status and associated factors among infants and young children aged 6–23 months in Yeka sub-city, Ethiopia, 2021. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted in selected health centres found in the Yeka sub-city from May 2021 to July 2021.

pmc-11444694.title: Deux cas de zona atypique chez des personnes prenant des inhibiteurs de Janus kinases par voie orale
pmc-11444694.creator: Rebecca Green, Elaine C Dupuis, Justin C Chia
pmc-11444694.description: ée pour traiter différentes affections inflammatoires et autoimmunes, ainsi que le cancer. Les médicaments immunosuppresseurs peuvent accroître le risque de réactivation du virus varicelle-zona (VZV), et les inhibiteurs de JAK comme l’upadacitinib sont associés à un risque accru de réactivation du VZV.

pmc-11500482.title: Psychosocial work environment in Swedish primary healthcare: a cross-sectional survey of physicians’ job satisfaction, turnover intention, social support, leadership climate and change fatigue
pmc-11500482.creator: Hanna Fernemark, Nadine Karlsson, Janna Skagerström, Ida Seing, Elin Karlsson, Emma Brulin, Per Nilsen
pmc-11500482.description: BackgroundPrimary healthcare, the first line of care in many countries, treats patients with diverse health problems. High workload, time pressure, poor job control and negative interpersonal experiences with supervisors have been documented in primary healthcare. The work environment in primary healthcare is also affected by several types of changes.

pmc-11611180.title: Exploring risk and protective factors of intimate partner violence in Korean young adults
pmc-11611180.creator: Soonok An, Jisoo Youn, Qihao Zhan, Soo-Jung Byoun
pmc-11611180.description: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is most prevalent in young adults, yet scarce evidence is available regarding South Korean young adults’ experience of IPV and culturally tailored IPV prevention programs. To address this gap, this study aimed to holistically assess IPV victimization and perpetration rates and the related risk and protective factors among Korean young adults.

pmc-12399517.title: Impact of trauma level designation on mortality in trauma patients with sepsis: an observational study across US trauma centers
pmc-12399517.creator: Ralphe Bou Chebl, Razan Diab, Reem Siblini, Rana Bachir, Mazen El Sayed
pmc-12399517.description: BackgroundSepsis is a major complication in trauma patients, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the varying resource allocation across trauma center levels, the impact of trauma center designation on sepsis-related mortality remains unclear. This study examines the association between trauma center level and sepsis outcomes in trauma patients using data from the National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) 2017 dataset.

pmc-12430508.title: Maternal Adverse Childhood Experiences and Delayed Initiation of Complementary Foods: A Nationwide Online Cohort Study
pmc-12430508.creator: Yousuke Imanishi, Ichiro Wada, Sinchul Jwa, Mai Uchida, Takahiro Tabuchi, Robert D Roghair
pmc-12430508.description: Background/Objectives: Infant feeding is critical for health and development, yet the influence of maternal psychosocial factors on its timing is not fully understood. While maternal adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are known to affect perinatal outcomes, their impact on the specific timing of initiating formula and complementary foods remains under-investigated.

pmc-12505734.title: The effect of cognitive behavioral therapy on depressive symptoms in parents of children with special needs: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12505734.creator: Ying Guo, Jiajun Lan, Haoran He
pmc-12505734.description: ObjectiveThis study conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluate the effects of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) on depressive symptoms in parents of children with special needs. Additionally, it examines potential moderators of treatment outcomes, including the type of child diagnosis and the dosage of intervention.

pmc-12559425.title: Impairment of lysosomal quality control in Huntington disease
pmc-12559425.creator: Paola Rusmini, Francesco Mina, Marta Valenza, Martina Vitali, Veronica Ferrari, Barbara Tedesco, Elena Casarotto, Marta Cozzi, Marta Chierichetti, Ali Mohamed, Paola Pramaggiore, Laura Cornaggia, Carmelo Milioto, Maria Brodnanova, Rocio Magdalena, Prashant Koshal, Margherita Piccolella, Riccardo Cri
pmc-12559425.description: Huntington disease (HD) is a neurodegenerative disease caused by a polyglutamine expansion (polyQ) in the Huntingtin protein (muHTT), which makes it prone to misfolding and aggregation. muHTT aggregates sequester a wide variety of proteins essential for cell homeostasis, including chaperones and transcription factors, and their depletion may contribute to HD pathogenesis.

pmc-12727893.title: Pregnancy and reproductive healthcare among adolescent girls in the child welfare system
pmc-12727893.creator: Sarah Font, Beatriz De Araujo Silva, Dylan Jones
pmc-12727893.description: ObjectiveThis study examines the prevalence and predictors of first pregnancy and the use of long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) among adolescent girls aged 12–17 involved in the child welfare system.MethodsThe study leverages linked longitudinal administrative data from the child welfare, juvenile legal, and Medicaid claims systems of Pennsylvania.

pmc-13093285.title: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression in tubo‐ovarian and endometrial tumors: a study of 923 cases
pmc-13093285.creator: Isabela Töltési, Kristýna Němejcová, Michaela Kendall Bártů, Romana Vránková, David Cibula, Pavel Fabian, Filip Frühauf, Jitka Hausnerová, Jan Laco, Gábor Méhes, Zuzana Špůrková, Marián Švajdler, Radoslav Matěj, Pavel Dundr
pmc-13093285.description: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) is a promising therapeutic target due to its high expression in several tumor types and its rare expression in healthy tissue. Recently, the antibody‐drug conjugate mirvetuximab soravtansine has been approved for treatment of advanced platinum‐resistant high‐grade serous carcinoma (HGSC).

pmc-13521889.title: The role of metacognition in fibromyalgia impact and psychological distress: a cross-sectional study in Turkish women with fibromyalgia

pmc-13685378.title: S. carcinoma arising in a breast implant: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-13685378.creator: Gustavo Adolfo Villegas-Gomez, Valentina Pérez-Ariza, Marcela Mejía-Arango, María Isabel Rizo
pmc-13685378.description: BackgroundBreast implants are widely used in plastic surgery and generally considered safe. However, recent reports of implant-associated malignancies, including anaplastic large-cell lymphoma and squamous-cell carcinoma, have raised concern. This report presents a case of squamous-cell carcinoma arising in a silicone breast implant and reviews the current literature on its association with breast implants.
